title: Northgate Freight: Cargo Loss and Damage Claims Handling, Business Requirements Document
labelStatus: author-labelled while writing the synthetic document; cross-checked by two independent blind AI reviewers; disagreements judged by an AI and each judgement confirmed by a person (#2255)
sections: Northgate Freight: Cargo Loss and Damage Claims Handling, Business Requirements Document
3.1 In scope for the first release
3.2 Out of scope for the first release

requirements.span: A handler shall be able to register a claim from an email, a telephone note passed on by customer service, or a completed claim form, and the application shall record the channel and the date and time the claim was first notified.

The application shall require the consignment note number when a claim is registered and shall retrieve the consignment's details from the operational tracking system, including the collection and delivery dates, the depots it passed through, any exceptions recorded and the proof of delivery.

If the consignment note number cannot be found in the tracking system, the handler shall be able to register the claim with the consignment marked as unverified, and the application shall prevent any payment on the claim until the consignment has been verified.
A single claim shall be able to cover several consignments for the same claimant, and the application shall record the loss type and amount claimed separately for each consignment.
The application shall warn the handler when a new claim is registered for a consignment that already has an open or closed claim, and shall show the existing claim.
The application shall calculate, for each consignment on a claim, whether the claim was notified within the time limit in the claimant's terms, and shall flag any claim notified late.
Under the standard conditions, damage and shortage must be notified within 7 days of delivery and loss within 28 days of the expected delivery date.
A late-notified claim shall not be rejected automatically; the handler shall record whether the time limit is being enforced and, if it is waived, the reason for the waiver.
The application shall maintain the list of documents required for each loss type, and the claims operations manager shall be able to change the list without a software release.
When a claim is registered, the application shall generate a request to the claimant listing the documents required for each consignment on the claim.

A handler shall be able to attach documents to a claim from email, from a file, or by forwarding an email to a claim-specific address, and the application shall record who attached each document and when.
The application shall not allow a claim to proceed to approval until every required document has been received or the handler has recorded why it is not needed.

If the required documents have not been received 21 days after the request, the application shall send a reminder to the claimant, and if they have still not been received 21 days after the reminder, the claim shall be closed as abandoned.
An abandoned claim can be reopened if the documents arrive later.
The handler shall be able to request an independent inspection for a damage claim, record the surveyor appointed, and attach the surveyor's report.
An inspection shall be requested for every damage claim on a high-value consignment before liability is decided.

The handler shall record a liability decision for each consignment on a claim, chosen from accepted, partly accepted or declined, with a reason chosen from a list maintained by the claims operations manager.
Where the liability decision is declined or partly accepted on the grounds of inadequate packaging, the handler shall attach the evidence supporting that decision before the decision can be saved.
The application shall show the handler the depot exceptions recorded for the consignment, so that the handler can see where in the network the loss or damage was first recorded.
Where the consignment was carried by a subcontracted haulier on any leg, the application shall identify the haulier and the leg from the tracking system and shall record them on the claim.
The application shall calculate the limit of liability for each consignment from the weight of the goods lost or damaged and the per-kilogram limit in the claimant's terms.
Where the claimant declared a value for the consignment and paid the declared value charge, the limit of liability shall be the declared value instead of the per-kilogram limit.

Where special terms apply, the application shall use the limits in the special terms, and the handler shall not be able to override the calculated limit without the approval of the claims operations manager.
The amount payable for a consignment shall be the lower of the proven value of the loss and the limit of liability, less any salvage value recovered from damaged goods.
The application shall show the handler how the amount payable was calculated, step by step, and the same explanation shall be included in the settlement letter to the claimant.

Consequential losses, such as lost profit or the cost of a missed production run, shall not be payable under the standard conditions, and the application shall prevent a handler from including them in the amount payable unless special terms allow them.
A delay claim shall only be payable where the claimant had a guaranteed delivery service, and the amount payable shall not exceed the carriage charge for the consignment.
The handler managing the claim can approve a settlement of up to 1,000.
A team leader on the regional desk must approve a settlement from 1,000 to 10,000.
The claims operations manager must approve a settlement from 10,000 to 50,000.
The finance director must approve a settlement above 50,000, after review by the legal department.
The application shall route each settlement to the approver required by the matrix and shall not allow a person to approve a settlement on a claim they registered or handled.
The approval limits in the matrix shall be configurable by the claims operations manager, and every change shall be recorded with the name of the person who made it and the date.
Once a settlement is approved, the application shall generate a settlement letter to the claimant showing the amount payable for each consignment and how it was calculated.

The application shall send an approved payment to the finance ledger as a payment instruction with the claimant's account details, and shall record the payment reference when finance confirms the payment.
A claimant shall be able to accept the settlement or dispute it, and a disputed settlement shall return to the handler with the claimant's reasons.
A claim shall be closed when every consignment on it has been paid, declined or withdrawn, and the application shall record the closing date and the outcome for each consignment.
When a claim is settled for a consignment carried by a subcontracted haulier, the application shall create a recovery case linked to the claim if the amount paid exceeds the recovery threshold.
The recovery case shall show the time limit for making the recovery claim under the haulier's subcontract and shall alert the recovery team 14 days before it expires.

The recovery team shall be able to record the amount claimed from the haulier, the haulier's response, and the amount recovered, and the application shall show the net cost of the original claim after recovery.
The recovery team shall be able to deduct an agreed recovery amount from the next payment to the haulier, and the application shall send the deduction to the finance ledger as an instruction.

The application shall identify every settled claim whose amount paid exceeds the insurance policy excess and shall produce, for any period, the schedule of those claims in the format the insurer requires.
The application shall record the amount recovered from the insurer against each claim in the schedule.
The application shall send the claimant an email when their claim is registered, when documents are requested, when liability is decided, when a settlement is approved and when the claim is closed.
Every message to the claimant shall quote the claim reference and the name of the handler managing the claim, and shall be sent from an address to which the claimant can reply.
Replies from claimants shall be attached to the claim automatically and the handler shall be notified.
Customer service staff shall be able to see the status of any claim and its history of messages, but shall not be able to change a claim.

The application shall report, for any period and by region, the number of claims notified, the number settled, the average time from notification to settlement, the total amount claimed, the total amount paid and the total amount recovered.
The application shall report the claims that have been open for more than 30 days, with the stage each one is at and how long it has been at that stage.
The application shall report recovery cases whose time limit expires in the next 30 days and have not yet been submitted to the haulier.
Finance shall be able to reconcile the payments recorded in the ledger against the settlements approved in the application for any period.
Access to claims shall be restricted by role, and handlers shall see the claims of every region so that work can be moved between desks when one is busy.
Every change to a claim, including changes to amounts, liability decisions and approvals, shall be recorded with the person who made it and the date and time, and the record shall not be editable.
Claim records and their documents shall be retained for seven years after the claim is closed and then deleted, unless the claim is subject to litigation.
The legal department has asked that access to documents be no wider than access to claims.
All claims open on the regional spreadsheets at go-live shall be migrated into the application with their status, amounts and the documents held in the mailbox.
Claims closed in the twelve months before go-live shall be migrated so that duplicate claim warnings and reporting cover them.
The application shall be available during the claims desks' working hours, from 7am to 7pm on working days, at least 99.5% of the time.
The application shall support at least 40 concurrent users without any page taking more than three seconds to load.
The application shall be usable by handlers working from home through the company's standard remote access arrangements.

ambiguities.description: the business rules summary gives 14 days for notice of damage and shortage while R7 gives 7 days; the summary says the capability sections take precedence but also that it predates legal review
ambiguities.question: Is the notice period for damage and shortage 7 days or 14 days after delivery?
spans: Within 14 days of delivery
Under the standard conditions, damage and shortage must be notified within 7 days of delivery and loss within 28 days of the expected delivery date.

ambiguities.description: the recovery threshold that triggers a recovery case is not defined
ambiguities.question: What claim amount must be exceeded before a recovery case is created against a haulier?
spans: The recovery threshold below which a recovery is not worth pursuing has not been agreed between finance and the recovery team.
When a claim is settled for a consignment carried by a subcontracted haulier, the application shall create a recovery case linked to the claim if the amount paid exceeds the recovery threshold.

ambiguities.description: "high-value consignment" is used as the trigger for mandatory inspection but is never defined
ambiguities.question: What makes a consignment high-value for mandatory inspection: the amount claimed, a declared value, the goods type, or something else?
spans: The definition of a high-value consignment for the purpose of mandatory inspection is still to be agreed with the legal department.
An inspection shall be requested for every damage claim on a high-value consignment before liability is decided.

ambiguities.description: approvers are to deal with approvals "promptly", with no target time and no escalation when they do not
ambiguities.question: How quickly must an approver act on a settlement, and what happens when they do not?
spans: Approvers are expected to deal with approvals promptly so that settlement times can be met.
The application shall route each settlement to the approver required by the matrix and shall not allow a person to approve a settlement on a claim they registered or handled.

ambiguities.description: the approval bands overlap at exactly 1,000, 10,000 and 50,000, so it is unclear who approves a settlement of exactly those amounts
ambiguities.question: Who approves a settlement of exactly 1,000, 10,000 or 50,000?
spans: The handler managing the claim can approve a settlement of up to 1,000.
A team leader on the regional desk must approve a settlement from 1,000 to 10,000.

ambiguities.description: a disputed settlement returns to the handler, but nothing says whether it needs re-approval, how many times it can be disputed, or when a dispute ends
ambiguities.question: After a claimant disputes a settlement, does a revised offer need approval again, and is there a limit on disputes or a final position?
spans: A claimant shall be able to accept the settlement or dispute it, and a disputed settlement shall return to the handler with the claimant's reasons.

ambiguities.description: a claim closed as abandoned can be reopened, but there is no rule on how late it can be reopened or whether the notification time limits still apply
ambiguities.question: Is there a deadline after which an abandoned claim can no longer be reopened?
spans: If the required documents have not been received 21 days after the request, the application shall send a reminder to the claimant, and if they have still not been received 21 days after the reminder, the claim shall be closed as abandoned.
A claim shall be closed when every consignment on it has been paid, declined or withdrawn, and the application shall record the closing date and the outcome for each consignment.

ambiguities.description: handlers see every region's claims, while legal asks that document access be no wider than claim access and the role model is not described; it is unclear whether customer service sees documents
ambiguities.question: Which roles may see the documents attached to a claim, including invoices and photographs of people?
spans: Access to claims shall be restricted by role, and handlers shall see the claims of every region so that work can be moved between desks when one is busy.
Customer service staff shall be able to see the status of any claim and its history of messages, but shall not be able to change a claim.

ambiguities.description: a claim covers several consignments but the approval matrix uses the total amount on the claim; it is not said whether splitting consignments across claims is prevented
ambiguities.question: Should the approval level be based on the claim total, and how is a claim split into several claims to stay under a limit prevented?
spans: A single claim shall be able to cover several consignments for the same claimant, and the application shall record the loss type and amount claimed separately for each consignment.
The application shall route each settlement to the approver required by the matrix and shall not allow a person to approve a settlement on a claim they registered or handled.

ambiguities.description: deducting a recovery from a haulier's next payment has no stated rule for a disputed recovery or a haulier with no further payments due
ambiguities.question: Can a recovery be deducted from a haulier's payment while the haulier disputes it, and what happens when no further payment is due?
spans: The recovery team shall be able to deduct an agreed recovery amount from the next payment to the haulier, and the application shall send the deduction to the finance ledger as an instruction.

The recovery team shall be able to record the amount claimed from the haulier, the haulier's response, and the amount recovered, and the application shall show the net cost of the original claim after recovery.

ambiguities.description: whether customer service may register claims directly is undecided, which changes who can perform R1
ambiguities.question: May customer service staff register claims themselves, or must they continue to pass them to the claims mailbox?
spans: A handler shall be able to register a claim from an email, a telephone note passed on by customer service, or a completed claim form, and the application shall record the channel and the date and time the claim was first notified.

ambiguities.description: delay claims are payable up to the carriage charge with a guaranteed service, while consequential losses are excluded; the document does not say whether delay compensation counts as a consequential loss under special terms
ambiguities.question: For a delay claim under special terms, is compensation still capped at the carriage charge, and is any delay loss treated as consequential?
spans: A delay claim shall only be payable where the claimant had a guaranteed delivery service, and the amount payable shall not exceed the carriage charge for the consignment.

Consequential losses, such as lost profit or the cost of a missed production run, shall not be payable under the standard conditions, and the application shall prevent a handler from including them in the amount payable unless special terms allow them.

ambiguities.description: the policy excess amount and whether it varies by policy or period is not given
ambiguities.question: What is the excess, and how is it maintained in the application?
spans: The application shall identify every settled claim whose amount paid exceeds the insurance policy excess and shall produce, for any period, the schedule of those claims in the format the insurer requires.

ambiguities.description: proven value and how salvage value is determined and recorded are not defined
ambiguities.question: What evidence establishes proven value, and how is salvage value captured?
spans: The amount payable for a consignment shall be the lower of the proven value of the loss and the limit of liability, less any salvage value recovered from damaged goods.

ambiguities.description: the customer claim form is never described, and the portal is out of scope, so its format and submission route are unclear
ambiguities.question: What is the claim form, in what format does it arrive, and what fields does it hold?
spans: A handler shall be able to register a claim from an email, a telephone note passed on by customer service, or a completed claim form, and the application shall record the channel and the date and time the claim was first notified.

ambiguities.description: usable and standard remote access arrangements are not defined or measurable
ambiguities.question: Which remote access method applies and what acceptance criteria define usable?
spans: The application shall be usable by handlers working from home through the company's standard remote access arrangements.

ambiguities.description: a handler can bypass the document gate by recording a reason, with no limit or approval
ambiguities.question: Are there document types that can never be waived, and does a waiver need approval?
spans: The application shall not allow a claim to proceed to approval until every required document has been received or the handler has recorded why it is not needed.

ambiguities.description: delay claims are in scope but no notification time limit is given for them, and the flag has no stated consequence or audience
ambiguities.question: What notice period applies to delay claims, and who sees the late flag?
spans: The application shall calculate, for each consignment on a claim, whether the claim was notified within the time limit in the claimant's terms, and shall flag any claim notified late.
